name: speaker_referring_production
summary: Speaker utterance production across 3-5 objects and 2-4 features with synonyms, testing how speaker models embedded in listener theories generalize to direct message choice.

charter.question: When participants act as speakers choosing a single referring word for a highlighted target object across scenes of varying complexity and synonym availability, do their utterance choices reflect bounded-depth literal informativeness, shared multi-cue object priors at depth 1 or depth 2, or feature-parsimony weighting?

instructions.welcome: Welcome! In this short study, you will play a communication game where you describe one target object to a listener.
instructions.task: On each turn, you and the listener see the same row of objects. One object is marked as your target. Your job is to choose one word from the list of available words that names a part on your target object so the listener can figure out which object is your target.

comprehension_checks.question: What is your job on each turn?
options: Choose one word that names a part on the marked target object so the listener can identify it
Choose a word for an object that is not the target
Click on every object in the row

comprehension_checks.question: Which words can describe the target object?
options: Words that name a part actually present on the target object
Only words for parts that the target object does not have
Any random word regardless of the target object
